facts.fact: The World Bank's appraisal document states that the civil registration system is outdated and still records on paper the ten acts of a person's life (birth, death and marriage among them); no date is given for the statement, so the document's publication date is used.

The World Bank says that in the urban areas of Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire digitalisation remains uneven across the civil registration centres, and that offices' access to broadband is uneven; it gives no count of offices or centres, and no date, so the document's publication date is used.

The World Bank describes the civil registration system as decentralised, operated by municipal officials and overseen by the Ministry of Territorial Administration, Decentralization and Local Development, with the justice and health ministries also involved; no date is given, so the document's publication date is used.

Sub-component 3.1 of the Congo Digital Acceleration Project, an IBRD loan of US$100 million appraised on 11 May 2022, allots US$11 million to modernising civil registration and the prerequisites of a digital ID: a technical assessment, an operational plan, a legal review, equipment to digitalise registration posts and a secure civil registration database; no domestic budget line is stated.

facts.fact: The World Bank's concept document, prepared 26 April 2021, states that in rural areas the civil registration system is largely paper-based and relies on manual processes, and calls the civil registration process as a whole decentralised and largely paper-based.

The World Bank states that in the civil registration centres of urban Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire no standardised system is used and, with no shared digital platform, electronic civil registry records are stored locally and not consolidated.

The World Bank says digitisation is uneven across the civil registration centres of urban Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire and that rural areas are largely paper-based; it gives no count or share of centres.

The World Bank states that the Government of Congo has developed a civil registration digitalisation roadmap to standardise the systems and create a consolidated population register; the roadmap's date and cost are not given.

facts.fact: The World Bank's digital economy diagnostic states that the civil status system is largely manual in rural areas; it gives no date for the statement, so the document's publication month is used.

The World Bank states that no standardised system is used in the civil status offices of urban Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire and that, with no web-based systems, registers are kept at municipal level with no consolidated information; no date is given, so the publication month is used.

The World Bank gives, as an example of uneven digitisation, that of Brazzaville's 10 civil status offices (9 arrondissements and 1 district) only 2 are digitised; no national count is given and no date, so the publication month is used.

The World Bank states that the Government, through the Ministry of the Interior, drew up the roadmap for digitising civil status and that a prototype of a consolidated system has been developed; no date is given, so the publication month is used.

The World Bank states that the Ministry of the Interior has drawn up a roadmap for the digitisation of civil status, to standardise the systems and create a consolidated civil status database; the roadmap's date and cost are not given, and the publication month is used.

The World Bank states that a prototype of a consolidated civil status system has been developed but its implementation in the offices is on hold because of budget constraints; no source of finance is named, and the publication month is used.
